summary: Moraga sits in a narrow valley tucked between two ridgelines of the East Bay hills, and that geography creates an unusual effect: a town of nearly 17,000 people that is almost entirely invisible from the surrounding region. There are essentially two roads in and two roads out, threading through Lamorinda's oak-studded canyons, which makes the place feel far more remote than its roughly 20-mile distance from downtown San Francisco would suggest. Saint Mary's College anchors the northern end, lending a faint college-town pulse to what is otherwise a deeply residential landscape — this is a textbook bedroom community, with most employment requiring a drive through the Caldecott Tunnel or down toward Walnut Creek. At a median home price near $1.6 million against a median household income just under $200,000, the price-to-income ratio hovers around 8:1, steep even by Bay Area standards, while rent at roughly $3,100 still claims about 19% of that median income — manageable for earners at that level, punishing for anyone well below it. The payoff is tangible: year-round highs averaging 67°F, over nine hours of daily sunshine, direct trail access into the vast East Bay Regional Park system, and property crime rates well below most comparably sized Bay Area cities. Moraga's defining tension is its seclusion — the same canyon geography that delivers golden-grass hillside views and quiet evenings also means every errand, every commute, and every restaurant meal involves navigating those two narrow corridors out.
